stories.title: Desperate late push to avert public-sector strike
stories.details: Despite an 11th-hour attempt at negotiations, a national public-sector strike scheduled for Wednesday appears increasingly inevitable. Both union representatives and government officials remain deadlocked, with neither side showing signs of backing down.

stories.title: IFS warns budget is a 'work of fiction'
stories.details: The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) has cautioned that the upcoming UK budget will lack credibility without a concrete plan to address £35bn in spending pressures. John Healey faces a difficult choice between raising taxes or implementing significant cuts to public services.

stories.title: UK inflation pressures hit three-year high
stories.details: A new report from BDO indicates that UK firms are facing their sharpest inflation pressures in three years, driven by rising energy, fuel, and raw material costs. Output in manufacturing and services has softened as businesses struggle with squeezed margins and plateauing growth.

stories.title: Failure to fit tags leaves 5,000 offenders unmonitored
stories.details: A new report reveals that a failure to properly fit electronic monitoring tags has left approximately 5,000 offenders unmonitored across England and Wales. The oversight has raised significant concerns regarding public safety and the efficacy of the current justice system.

stories.title: Andy Burnham claims Russian interference in Brexit
stories.details: Andy Burnham has stated that it is clear Russia interfered in the Brexit referendum. The comments add to the ongoing debate regarding foreign influence in UK democratic processes.

stories.title: Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine
stories.details: President Trump claimed that Russia and Ukraine had reached a truce regarding energy infrastructure attacks, but President Zelenskyy stated the deal was 'news to me.' Ukraine has previously rejected US calls to stop bombing Russian oil refineries, insisting that Moscow must end its own attacks on energy infrastructure first.

stories.title: Saudi and Yemeni airports hit by missile attacks
stories.details: Riyadh airport and the Yemeni capital were rocked by new missile strikes, resulting in at least two deaths. This follows a deadly Houthi strike in Riyadh that killed 12 people, marking the most lethal attack on a Gulf Arab country since the Iran war began.

stories.title: Europe breaks Taliban taboo
stories.details: European governments, previously shunning the Taliban due to human rights concerns, are now negotiating with the regime to facilitate the deportation of refugees. The Taliban view this engagement as a potential gateway to international acceptance five years after regaining power.

stories.title: Israeli election stakes rise
stories.details: Israel is heading to the polls in two weeks for the first time since the October 7 attacks. The election is framed as a critical juncture for the country's future, with voters divided over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership and the government's handling of security and judicial reforms.

stories.title: Manchester City defeat Liverpool
stories.details: Manchester City secured a victory over Liverpool in the second half of their match, with goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku, and Rayan Cherki. The win followed a red card for Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch, with manager Enzo Maresca praising his team's resilience.

stories.title: Ken Early: City fans embrace their club
stories.details: Columnist Ken Early reflects on the evolving relationship between Manchester City fans and their club. He argues that supporters are no longer forced to live a lie and are embracing the club for its true identity.

stories.title: Spectre of 'ghost football' at City
stories.details: Jonathan Wilson discusses the significance of Manchester City's recent win, noting the strange atmosphere surrounding the club's current performance. He questions the long-term implications of their recent tactical displays.

stories.title: Max Verstappen wins in Singapore
stories.details: Max Verstappen claimed victory in the Singapore Grand Prix, adding to his recent sprint triumph and success in Malaysia. The win serves as a warning to competitors for the 2027 season, though Kimi Antonelli remains in contention for the title in Austin.

stories.title: Irish provinces undercooked for Champions Cup
stories.details: Irish rugby provinces are reportedly looking undercooked ahead of the opening fixtures of the Champions Cup. Concerns have been raised regarding their readiness for the high-intensity European competition.

stories.title: Mater Hospital bans 33 patients
stories.details: The Mater Hospital in Dublin has banned 33 patients this year due to aggressive behavior. Fourteen of these exclusion orders were issued for physical assault, while the remainder were for verbal abuse or threats, including a knife threat against staff.

stories.title: Times Welfare Inquiry findings
stories.details: An investigation by The Times reveals that the UK government is paying sickness benefits to nearly two million people without knowing if they still qualify. The inquiry highlights a crisis in the benefits system, noting that the UK spends £40 on welfare transfers for every £1 spent helping people find work.

stories.title: Pope to undergo lung surgery
stories.details: Pope Leo XIV announced during his Sunday address that he will undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a localized, early-stage growth on his lung. The announcement was made from St Peter’s Square in the Vatican.
